payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_regate.py::test_regate_prints_a_version_that_only_raised_and_counts_it_nowhere stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/gates/core/witness.py. The claim was "`saffron regate` passes the assertion pattern of the policy it exported at the task's base to `_apply_criterion_probes`. A revived version that raised prints its own line, `regate: <spec> wrong version raised: <version> (<summary>)`, and adds no new failure. The witness builds the wrong-version fixture with `^KeyError` declared at the task's base and `^assert` at `main`. It calls `regate` with the task's own first version failed by an `assert` detail. The first two pair lines read `raised: v1` then `survived: v2`, and the last line counts three new failures. A second `regate` with a `KeyError` detail prints no raised line.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_session.py::test_a_drive_hands_review_its_policys_assertion_for_each_wrong_version, tests/test_session.py::test_a_witness_that_only_raises_under_an_edit_reads_raised_and_files_a_concern, tests/test_suite.py::test_the_suite_hands_witness_its_policys_assertion_and_a_raise_blocks_nothing, tests/test_witness_gate.py::test_a_witness_that_fails_only_by_raising_reads_as_raised_and_moves_no_status, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
